cards.text: Jacob, Isaac's son, has been working for Laban, his father-in-law. Rachel, one of Jacob's wives, has given birth to a son named Joseph. After that, Jacob walks up to Laban with something on his mind.

cards.question: Jacob has something to ask his father-in-law Laban. What is it?

answers.text: Send him on his way back home
Give him a field of his own
Let him build a house nearby

cards.question: Jacob plans to leave his wives and children behind with Laban and go home alone.

cards.text: Laban is NOT ready to let him go. He says, "If I have found favor in your eyes, please stay."

cards.question: Laban says he has learned by divination that the LORD has ___ him because of Jacob.

cards.text: Then Laban says, "Name your wages, and I will pay them." Friend, when the boss says NAME YOUR PRICE, you don't blink, you don't cough, you don't check your phone, you start TALKING.
And Jacob TALKS. He reminds Laban how he has served him and how Laban's livestock have thrived under his care, like a man walking into his yearly review with a folder full of receipts.

cards.question: Jacob tells Laban that he had very little before Jacob arrived, but now his wealth has increased many times over.

cards.text: Then Jacob asks, "But now, when may I also provide for my own household?" And Laban asks, "What can I give you?"

cards.question: Jacob says Laban doesn't need to give him anything. He'll keep shepherding Laban's flocks if Laban does one thing. What does Jacob want as his wages?

answers.text: The strongest rams in the flock
A tenth of every new lamb

cards.text: Jacob even spells it out: any goat of his that isn't speckled or spotted, or any lamb that isn't dark-colored, will be considered stolen. That's a man signing his name in PERMANENT MARKER.

cards.question: Jacob says his ___ will testify for him when Laban comes to check on his wages in the future.
After hearing all that, Laban turns down Jacob's offer.

cards.text: That very day, Laban himself removes every streaked, speckled or spotted goat, every one with any white on it, and every dark-colored lamb. No "let me sleep on it," no "I'll circle back," THAT VERY DAY.

cards.question: Laban has pulled all the spotted and dark-colored animals out of the flocks. Whose care does he put them under?

cards.text: Then Laban puts a three-day journey between himself and Jacob. Friend, I keep a little distance from a tray of burnt cookies too, but THREE DAYS? That's not distance, that's a whole new zip code.

Meanwhile, Jacob is out shepherding the rest of Laban's flocks. Then he grabs fresh branches of poplar, almond and plane trees and starts peeling off the bark, one branch at a time, like a man with a PLAN.

cards.question: Jacob peels the bark off the fresh branches. What does that leave showing?
Where does Jacob set the peeled branches, right in front of the flocks?

answers.text: Along the path to the field

cards.text: When the flocks are in heat and come to drink, they mate right there in front of those branches. Jacob put them where EVERYBODY has to show up, like taping your flyer to the elevator door.

cards.question: The young the flocks bear come out streaked or speckled or spotted.

cards.text: Jacob sets those young apart and turns the rest of the flock to face the streaked dark-colored sheep in Laban's flocks. This man is arranging sheep the way I arrange chocolate chips on a tray, EVERY ONE facing the right way.

cards.question: Jacob keeps his own stock mixed in with Laban's animals.

cards.text: And now Jacob gets PICKY. Whenever the stronger females are in heat, he puts the branches in the troughs, in full view, so they'll breed in front of them.

cards.question: If the animals were ___, Jacob did not set out the branches.
So the stronger animals go to Jacob, and the weaker ones go to Laban.
So how does all of this turn out for Jacob?

answers.text: He loses most of his flocks

cards.text: Large flocks, maidservants and menservants, camels AND donkeys. The man who asked when he could provide for his own household got his answer, but set this batch on the cooling rack, friend, because Jacob's story is still in the oven.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 1 quotes "let me sleep on it", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The correct answer changes Jacob's wage categories. Genesis 30:32 names every speckled or spotted sheep, every dark-colored lamb, and every spotted or speckled goat. "Every spotted and dark-colored animal" leaves the speckled category unstated and is broader than the dark-colored lambs.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The options mix different kinds of answers: "honesty" is an abstract quality, while "sons" and "servants" are people. The correct answer also stands out as the only option that is not a person or group of people.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the statement about the three-day journey, the burnt-cookie question, and the zip-code punchline. It needs to be shortened to one or two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
